historical_metadata_R0011.title: Lifting curved Kakeya sets to linear Kakeya sets
historical_metadata_R0011.visual_check: Pages 1 and 4 rendered with Poppler and inspected; legible. Font type mismatch warnings did not prevent these renders.
read_scope: Introduction, definitions and main statements, pp.1-7
claims_checked: An (s,nu)-lift requires a coherent ruling family and slope rank n+s-1-nu, with slopes independent of the curve intercept w.
Proposition 2.2 gives d_Kak(X) >= d_lin(n+s-nu)-s, a forward implication from a higher-dimensional straight-line input.
For X_B=w+(tI+t^2B)y, Proposition 2.5(i) gives (s,nu)=(rank B,rank B-rank B^2).
Theorem 1.3 is conditional on straight-line Kakeya in dimension n+rank B^2; it is not itself a proof in those dimensions.
For n=3 and invertible 2x2 B the displayed standard lift uses straight-line dimension 5; the scalar B exception can instead be straightened by a time change.
